move: macOS widget rises, tasks tick off with strikethroughs, ring fills quarters
how: A sunset wallpaper slowly zooms (scale 1.06 to 1.1, linear) under a frosted-glass widget that rises in with power3.out; dock icons pop with back.out(2) and four task rows slide in from x 16. From 18%, every 0.7s, a task completes: its circle scales 1.25 yoyo and fills orange, a check fades in, the label dims to 45% and a strikethrough line scales x 0 to 1 with power3.out, while the ring arc grows a quarter (stroke-dasharray via expo.out proxy tween) and the centre number ticks 0 to 4. At 60% the ring bumps scale 1.06. From 86% the checks, fills, strikes and ring unwind so the tasks are open again, but the widget itself stays on screen.
adapt: Replace the four task names, the title and subtitle, the orange (#ff7a3d) and the wallpaper; the ring fraction is derived from task count; keep the 0.7s task cadence and the expo.out ring step.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the widget, appends the strike em elements and the dock; animate returns the timeline with the widget entry at 0, ticks at 0.18D + i*0.14D and the unwind at 0.86D. The '--f' and '--s' custom-property tweens do nothing visible and can be dropped; scope querySelectorAll('.it') to el.
caveats: loop does not close cleanly: the widget enters from opacity 0 at frame 0 but is still visible on the last frame
backdrop-filter blur on the widget, menu bar and dock
the --f/--s CSS variable tweens are dead code, the ::after pseudo-elements never animate
